    <head>
        <title>Swagger UI: OAuth2 Redirect</title>
    </head>
    <body>
    <script>
        'use strict';
        function run () {
            var oauth2 = window.opener.swaggerUIRedirectOauth2;
            var sentState = oauth2.state;
            var redirectUrl = oauth2.redirectUrl;
            var isValid, qp, arr;

            if (/code|token|error/.test(window.location.hash)) {
                qp = window.location.hash.substring(1).replace('?', '&');
            } else {
                qp = location.search.substring(1);
            }

            arr = qp.split("&");
            arr.forEach(function (v,i,_arr) { _arr[i] = '"' + v.replace('=', '":"') + '"';});
            qp = qp ? JSON.parse('{' + arr.join() + '}',
                    function (key, value) {
                        return key === "" ? value : decodeURIComponent(value);
                    }
            ) : {};

            isValid = qp.state === sentState;

            if ((
              oauth2.auth.schema.get("flow") === "accessCode" ||
              oauth2.auth.schema.get("flow") === "authorizationCode" ||
              oauth2.auth.schema.get("flow") === "authorization_code"
            ) && !oauth2.auth.code) {
                if (!isValid) {
                    oauth2.errCb({
                        authId: oauth2.auth.name,
                        source: "auth",
                        level: "warning",
                        message: "Authorization may be unsafe, passed state was changed in server. The passed state wasn't returned from auth server."
                    });
                }

                if (qp.code) {
                    delete oauth2.state;
                    oauth2.auth.code = qp.code;
                    oauth2.callback({auth: oauth2.auth, redirectUrl: redirectUrl});
                } else {
                    let oauthErrorMsg;
                    if (qp.error) {
                        oauthErrorMsg = "["+qp.error+"]: " +
                            (qp.error_description ? qp.error_description+ ". " : "no accessCode received from the server. ") +
                            (qp.error_uri ? "More info: "+qp.error_uri : "");
                    }

                    oauth2.errCb({
                        authId: oauth2.auth.name,
                        source: "auth",
                        level: "error",
                        message: oauthErrorMsg || "[Authorization failed]: no accessCode received from the server."
                    });
                }
            } else {
                oauth2.callback({auth: oauth2.auth, token: qp, isValid: isValid, redirectUrl: redirectUrl});
            }
            window.close();
        }

        if (document.readyState !== 'loading') {
            run();
        } else {
            document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
                run();
            });
        }
    </script>
    </body>

Holds no values from the data. Needs no client. Call it before data_query, and never invent a column name: if the catalog has no column for the question, say so.

search.description: A word to find in names and descriptions.

tools.name: data_query
tools.description: Structured, read-only query over ONE client's payroll and enriched calculation data (needs a client). Use it only for questions the fixed tools (client_eligibility, client_trend, client_at_risk, simulate and the rest) cannot answer: descriptive or comparative questions such as an average, a count or a total by location, month, year, designation or method. For anything about the credit figure, eligibility or what the engine concluded, the fixed tools are authoritative; this tool returns exact rows and aggregates from the data, it does not interpret them. Read data_catalog first and use its names exactly, never an invented column; use data_distinct_values to find a location or code before filtering on it. Name every measure with `as` (for example `average_headcount`): the answer refers to a result column by that name. Never write SQL. Prefer an aggregate to a long list: a result is capped (default 100 rows, at most 500) and says when it was cut. Rows that describe individual employees go to the person asking only; Copilot Cowork refuses them unless the user is a writer.

rules.name: Tennessee Job Tax Credit
rules.prototype_verification: PROTOTYPE rule pack. Core parameters VERIFIED against T.C.A. § 67-4-2109 (2024 Tennessee Code, via Justia — see _sources): base Job Tax Credit = $4,500 per qualified job, statewide, for making the $500,000 required capital investment AND creating at least 25 qualified jobs (reduced to 20 jobs in a tier 3, and 10 jobs in a tier 4, enhancement county). A qualified job = a permanent position of at least 37.5 hours/week for 12 consecutive months; part-time (>=20 hrs/wk) and seasonal (>=26 wks) each count as 0.5 job. Enhancement counties (tier 2/3/4) earn an ADDITIONAL annual credit of $4,500/job for 3-5 years. Unused credit carries forward 15 years (25 years for credits earned in tax years ending on/after 12/31/2008). Per the partner (7/9/26) eligibility is STATEWIDE (no pinpointer gate); geography changes the dollar value only. The weekly-WAGE floor is NOT in the statute (it requires 37.5 hrs + minimum health care) and remains _prototype_verify pending the partner. NOTE: a post-7/1/2025 version of the statute exists; confirm the current text before client use.

findings.title: Employee counted at two worksites in one month — clear-cut
findings.why_it_matters: The engine counts headcount per unit, so a person appearing at two worksites in the same month is counted twice. That inflates Average Headcount, which inflates the credit. In these one worksite holds at least 75% of the month's hours, so which unit owns the head is arithmetic rather than a judgement.
findings.proposed_effect: Counts each employee at their dominant worksite for that month.
